title.narrative: Integrated Health Program (IHP) Task Order Six (TO6)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Scale up high impact interventions in 171 primary health care units A(PHCs), 27 private/mission health facilities, and 14 secondary health facilities; .Expand access to integrated reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, adolescent health and nutrition (RMNCAH+N) services and bring services closer to communities;.Support monthly joint supportive supervisory visits with the Local Government Health Authority tailored to priority PHCs; .Provide technical support to relevant agencies to effectively implement the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund and the State Health Equity Fund to reach the most vulnerable with basic health services; and.Focus on skills transfer to strengthen the quality of services, data quality and use, and commodities management through clinical mentoring, coaching and support nutrition specific actions within the health facilities and outreach programs in communities.. Integrate WASH activities into health programming to support maternity services and improved service delivery..This activity will contribute to reductions in child and maternal morbidity and mortality and increase the capacity of health systems (public and private) to sustainably support quality PHC services for RMNCAH+N in Ebonyi State as part of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed between USAID and the State government on PHC revitalization. It will work in 13 Local Government Areas and support the state to update a harmonized 2023 annual operational plan based on prior performance reviews and lessons learned and will include evidence-based budgeting for 2023. This activity contributes to USAID priorities by focusing on evidence-based interventions, sustainability, localization and capacity building. It contributes to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the Embassy's ICS, and is closely aligned with Goal 3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan..
